source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"They are pulmonary-function measures used primarily to quantify ventilation and gas exchange","B":"They are cardiac-specific tests used primarily to diagnose acute myocardial injury and infarction","C":"They can contribute information about nutritional status and some liver, kidney, or protein disorders","D":"They directly measure long-term glycemic control in the same way as hemoglobin A1c testing"}}
source_row.rationale: Total protein and the A/G ratio can aid evaluation of nutritional status and conditions affecting liver function, kidney protein loss, immune proteins, or other systemic processes. They are not cardiac-specific tests.
source_row.source_detail: Clinical uses and interpretation of total protein and A/G ratio; U.S. National Library of Medicine; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: MedlinePlus — Total Protein and Albumin/Globulin (A/G) Ratio
source_row.stem: A client asks why total protein and the albumin/globulin ratio were ordered. Which explanation is most appropriate?
